name: Projective plane order 12
question: Does a finite projective plane of order 12 exist?
first_attack: Certify constructions or automate nonexistence for constrained automorphism classes
dispatch_next: Encode order-12 planes with a prescribed collineation as SAT with DRAT proof output, starting from cases the literature already excludes.
dispatch_why: The next experiment encodes literature-excluded collineation cases with a proof trace. Unconstrained search of order 12 is the blocker, not the plan.

campaign.method: Incidence-axiom certificates, Bruck-Ryser sieve and constrained exhaustive search
campaign.hypothesis: Decide whether a finite projective plane of order 12 exists.
campaign.first_proof_obligation: Reproduce a published partial nonexistence result for order 12 (for example a restriction on collineations) before any search.
campaign.next_experiment: Encode order-12 planes with a prescribed collineation as SAT with DRAT proof output, starting from cases the literature already excludes.
campaign.falsification: An explicit order-12 incidence structure passing the combinatorial axiom check would settle existence.
campaign.blocker: Unconstrained search is far out of reach; the order-10 nonexistence proof needed a massive computation.

probes.name: Projective plane order 12
probes.title: Projective planes of prime-power order and the Bruck-Ryser order sieve
probes.frontier: Known: order 10 excluded by computer search (Lam, Thiel & Swiercz 1989); 12 is the smallest order whose existence is open. Every known plane has prime-power order.

smoke.scope: PG(2,q) satisfies the projective-plane axioms for every prime power q <= 9; Bruck-Ryser classification of every order n <= 50.

deep.scope: PG(2,q) satisfies the projective-plane axioms for every prime power q <= 27; Bruck-Ryser classification of every order n <= 200.

milestones.title: Projective planes of every prime-power order <= 9 and the Bruck-Ryser table to 50
milestones.scope: Known constructions and exclusions; order 12 remains open
milestones.description: PG(2,q) incidence axioms verified combinatorially; Bruck-Ryser exclusions recomputed by brute-force sums of two squares; deep run to q = 27 and orders <= 200.

formal_statement.encodes: No incidence relation on 157 points and 157 lines with 13 points per line, unique joining lines and unique meeting points.

kernel_checked.claim: The axioms are satisfiable: planes of orders 2 (Fano) and 3 exist (exists_order_2, exists_order_3).
